==Problem==

The Centerville Middle School chess team consists of two boys and three girls. A photographer wants to take a picture of the team to appear in the local newspaper. She decides to have them sit in a row with a boy at each end and the three girls in the middle. How many such arrangements are possible?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }2\qquad\textbf{(B) }4\qquad\textbf{(C) }5\qquad\textbf{(D) }6\qquad \textbf{(E) }12</imath>

==Solution==
There are <imath>2! = 2</imath> ways to order the boys on the ends, and there are <imath>3!=6</imath> ways to order the girls in the middle. We get the answer to be <imath>2 \cdot 6 = \boxed{\textbf{(E) }12}</imath>.
